summary: Fossil occurrences with ages are open (PBDB: Foraminifera taxon record with 196,776 occurrences, 6,711 in 'siz', 1,478 in 'exs'), molecular sequences are open (GenBank 315,003 records; PR2), and planktonic shell images/morphometrics are open (Zenodo 165514, 7898373). What is missing is a coded shell-form character matrix for foraminifera and a combined fossil-plus-molecular tree with the forms mapped; the planktonic subset is the tractable scope, and benthic molecular coverage was not measured.
next_step: Define 'identical form' as classes of a published chamber-arrangement scheme, code them for a set of genera from pforams@mikrotax or PBDB, and map them onto a PR2- or GenBank-derived tree.
obstacles_confirmed: What counts as an 'identical form' depends on the morphological resolution chosen.
Molecular trees are dense for planktonic clades and sparse for long-ranging benthic groups.
Many benthic genera are still classified by the shell form whose homology is in question.
